Disposition: WHOLE_PASS_BOUNDED_RESULT_ONLY_COMPOSE_APPLIED / PAPER_PASS_BOUNDED_NEW_WHOLE_SCOPE_ONLY. Mathematical must-fix items: 0. Reviewer-supplied construction, repair, or author-proof changes: 0.

This is one genuine independent review of the entire new A-authored 19286-byte artifact, all eight sections, equations (1)-(18), actual-input history, authorship chronology and stopping boundary. It accepts the counterexample to the stronger actual-site conformal lifting method, its complete three-state fiber, and its legal ordered two-step path. It does not accept a universal connectivity or impossibility theorem for the two-axis palette. The review's own Source publication and ordinary author reception are PENDING at creation.

## 1. Precise model, conclusion, and genuinely necessary inputs

The fixed chart and seven full joint coset readouts remain literal: the six coordinate-line coset sums retain the other five coordinates jointly, and the seventh sums on cosets of the primitive all-ones diagonal. States are integer N0 arrays supported in

    B = {0,1,2,3}^2 x {0,1,2}^4.

An actual path stays within this box and is nonnegative at every actual six-coordinate site at every step. It is an auxiliary finite graph path, without a Native time/evolution interpretation. The first two coordinates use x,y; the remaining four use Z_1,...,Z_4. The definitions are

    U = product Z_i, A = product (Z_i-1), T=(x-1)(y-1),
    Phi(H)=(xyU-1)HA, G=Phi(T), L(H)=(xy-1)H.

The old accepted13283 supplies the complete integer boxed kernel, not merely some polynomial generators: every zero-readout integer array in B is uniquely GQ, with Q separately of degree at most one in x and y and no Z dependence. Its H=TQ is a 3-by-3 integer table with zero row and column sums. The reviewer has now personally whole-read that complete old source for the first time, including its full integer-kernel proof, actual-site map, mass93 two-state theorem, context and exclusions. It was only opaque commit metadata during the earlier long-axis review; that historical boundary is not rewritten.

The earlier accepted19788 boxed author and its original true peer16885 were genuinely whole-read by this reviewer in the later global-library intake, after the earlier temporary long-axis chat review. Their own actual Source returns and semantic whole consumption are honestly reused. No new old19788 call or compare is claimed now. The input19788 has its original single-long-axis box; its actual sign-conformal sufficient mechanism is not a theorem for this new two-axis box or for every member of the later all-d long-axis family.

A simple transportation cycle here is a simple cycle of the bipartite row/column graph on the 3-by-3 table: four or six nonzero alternating unit entries. Both orientations are allowed. S is the finite palette of their actual Phi images, used one actual member at a time with the legal sign. No hidden multiples, batches, changed observer or changed positivity category are introduced.

The stronger method being tested would decompose every such H into cycles whose Phi images are each conformal to the total actual Phi(H). Actual conformality means site by site both compatible sign and magnitude at most that of the total; a zero site of the total forces zero in each conformal term. Table sign-conformality alone is insufficient. The accepted negative conclusion is a concrete failure of that stronger method.

## 2. Full integer and actual-site interfaces were checked

The old13283 integer Laurent proof uses the seven prime factors for the coordinate and diagonal readouts. Their quotient rings are integral Laurent domains. Each factor remains nonzero modulo each different one, so successive prime division gives their product, without a false comaximality premise or passage to Q. In the integral Laurent domain the extrema in each variable add under multiplication. Since G has extrema0 and2 in each coordinate, support in B forces exactly the stated four-parameter integer Q. Uniqueness follows from the domain property.

For the reverse table interface, a 3-by-3 integer table with zero row and column sums vanishes as a polynomial at x=1 and y=1. Successive monic division in Z[x,y] gives H=(x-1)(y-1)Q, with integer Q of separate degrees at most one. Thus the simple cycles really lift to supported zero-readout integer arrays. Phi is injective, again because its nonzero factors lie in a Laurent domain.

The overlap signs depend on the FOUR remaining axes. Both A and UA have coefficient +1 at e=(1,1,1,1); the old five-axis odd-overlap sign cannot be substituted. The exclusive lower and upper cubes each have15 sites, with7 positive and8 negative coefficients; both signs are actually present. Extending H by zero, the full actual-site map is

    lower exclusive: -epsilon_a H(i,j),
    upper exclusive:  gamma_b H(i-1,j-1),
    common e:         H(i-1,j-1)-H(i,j)=L(H)_(i,j).

All other transverse sites are zero. These three disjoint site types account for every actual coefficient, every later norm, and all nonnegativity checks. The reviewer checked the author against the same literal map in old13283, including the shifts, signs, boundaries and zero extension.

## 3. The fixed move and the actual conformal obstruction

The new table is

    H_*=(1+xy)T
       =1-x-y+2xy-x^2 y-xy^2+x^2 y^2,

with rows (1,-1,0), (-1,2,-1), (0,-1,1). It has zero row and column sums, L1 norm8, and seven nonzero positions. T+xyT is table-sign-conformal to H_*: the positive center coefficient2 is split into two positive units. Both summands are simple four-cycles, and their actual supports remain inside B.

The reviewer manually expanded the complete common-site polynomial:

    L(H_*)=-1+x+y-xy+x^2 y^2-x^3 y^2-x^2 y^3+x^3 y^3.

It has eight distinct unit terms; in particular the common positions (1,2) and (2,1) are zero. The lower table positions (0,2) and (2,0) are also zero. Disjoint site types give

    ||Phi(H_*)||_1 = 15*8+15*8+8 = 248.

Zero total follows from any zero coordinate readout. For P_*=Phi(H_*), its sign parts f=P_*^+ and g=P_*^- therefore both have mass124 and the same original O. This is the mass of this witness, not a claimed universal palette threshold.

For ANY integer actual kernel submove p conformal to P_*, the complete boxed kernel writes p=Phi(C), with C a zero-row/zero-column integer3-by-3 table. Zero lower sites force C_02=C_20=0. Zero common sites force C_01=C_12 and C_10=C_21. These are actual-site constraints, additional to table sign compatibility.

Set C_00=a. Row0 and column0 give C_01=C_10=-a. The common constraints then give C_12=C_21=-a. Row1 gives C_11=2a, and row2 gives C_22=a; the remaining column equations are consistent. Thus C=aH_*. At the lower exclusive site with table index(0,0) and transverse index(0,0,0,0), P_*=-1 and p=-a. The conformal sign and magnitude bounds force integer0<=a<=1. Hence the only conformal kernel submoves are0 and P_*.

This verifies actual-site conformal indecomposability, including signs, magnitudes and integer saturation. It is not computation or classification of a full Graver basis. A simple cycle image cannot be P_* because injectivity would identify its table with H_*, which has a coefficient2 and seven nonzero positions. Thus there is no nonzero conformal simple-cycle image at all, and a sum of such conformal images cannot equal P_*. Repeating cycles or reversing their orientation does not evade this obstruction.

## 4. Exhaustion of the entire N0 fiber

For any same-output state k in B, f-k=Phi(C) with C as above. At a lower exclusive site, nonnegativity is exactly

    max(-epsilon_a H_*(i,j),0)+epsilon_a C_ij >=0.

Both actual epsilon signs occur. At each table position this forces C_ij between0 and H_*(i,j) with the corresponding sign, and C_ij=0 where H_*=0. In particular a=C_00 and b=C_22 belong to{0,1}, C_02=C_20=0, and zero rows/columns determine

    C = [ a  -a    0 ]
        [-a a+b   -b ]
        [ 0  -b    b ] = aT+bxyT.

The central bound0<=a+b<=2 is automatic. These are necessary restrictions derived from real sites, not an assumption that every projected table is feasible.

At the two common sites (1,2,e) and (2,1,e), f is zero and L(C)=b-a. Therefore k>=0 forces b<=a. Only the integer pairs(0,0),(1,0),(1,1) remain. They give f, m=f-G, and g. No other candidate can survive.

The endpoints are actual sign parts. Feasibility of the middle candidate is separately paid at EVERY site type. At exclusive sites, table conformality of T to H_* and the literal signed map imply that subtracting G from f is nonnegative. At common sites the exact arrays are

    L(T)=-1+x+y-x^2y-xy^2+x^2y^2,
    f_common=x+y+x^2y^2+x^3y^3,
    m_common=f_common-L(T)=1+x^2y+xy^2+x^3y^3.

Every common coefficient is nonnegative, and all other transverse sites remain zero. Thus m really is a nonnegative state in B. Since G has all zero original readouts and zero total, m is in the same fiber and has mass124.

This proves the complete identity fiber_B(f)=fiber_B(g)={f,m,g}, not just a list of three examples. The lower inequalities exhausted all possible tables, the common inequalities removed(0,1), and the remaining candidate's full-site feasibility was proved explicitly.

## 5. Legal path, required temporary sites, and the precise negative scope

The actual differences are f-m=G=Phi(T) and m-g=xyG=Phi(xyT). Both are images of simple four-cycles in S. Their mass is63: ||T||_1=4 and ||L(T)||_1=6 give ||G||_1=15*4+15*4+6=126, and translation preserves the norm. The proved middle-state feasibility makes the ordered two-step path legal at every site, with no mass124 step needed.

The common sites(1,2,e) and(2,1,e) have value0 at BOTH endpoints and value1 at m. Hence the path leaves the coordinatewise interval between its endpoints while remaining in N0. Subtracting xyG first is illegal there: its common coefficients are+1 and f is zero. The order G first, xyG second is therefore a real positivity issue rather than interchangeable formal summation.

There is no direct S edge f-g: it would require a simple cycle table to equal H_*. Since the entire fiber has exactly three vertices and a direct edge is absent, every S path from f to g must pass through m. The temporary positive values at those zero-endpoint sites are necessary for a path in this particular palette and fiber.

The counterexample therefore falsifies universal actual-conformal cycle lifting. It simultaneously shows that S connects this whole particular fiber. It does not show S fails to connect every fiber, give an upper palette for the entire two-axis box, or prove a lower bound124 on the maximum move mass of a universal palette. The older mass93 indispensable-move theorem remains its own accepted bounded statement; no claimed sharpness at93 or124 is imported. No conclusion is drawn for larger boxes, more long axes, other coefficient/occupancy categories, or a physical dynamic.
